COLLABORATING WITH PUBLIC SAFETY – SLED 2025

This section outlines expectations and practices for collaborating with Public Safety in the context of SLED 2025. All residence life staff should understand how and when to work with Public Safety to support student safety, uphold community standards, and respond to incidents in and around the residence halls.

Collaboration with Public Safety under SLED 2025 includes:

- Recognizing Public Safety as a key partner in maintaining a safe and secure residential environment.
- Following all established SLED 2025 protocols when contacting or coordinating with Public Safety.
- Communicating clearly, promptly, and professionally with Public Safety officers during any incident response.
- Supporting Public Safety’s role while maintaining appropriate residence life responsibilities and boundaries.
- Ensuring that any required documentation, reporting, or follow-up related to Public Safety interactions is completed in accordance with SLED 2025 guidelines.

All staff are expected to be familiar with current SLED 2025 procedures and to apply them consistently when collaborating with Public Safety.

Collaboration with Campus Public Safety

Residence Life collaborates closely with Campus Safety & Security to support students and maintain a safe living environment in the residence halls. Campus Safety & Security is a student support resource and is distinct from the police. 

This collaboration focuses on:

- Campus safety and security needs within the halls  
- Responding to and addressing crimes that occur in the residence halls  
- Responding to and addressing policy violations in the residence halls  

By working together with Campus Safety & Security, Residence Life ensures that safety concerns, crimes, and policy violations in the halls are addressed promptly and appropriately while prioritizing student support.

Residence Life and Public Safety collaborate extensively beyond individual incidents through their joint involvement in the campus-wide Behavioral Intervention Team (BIT) and CARE Team. This partnership ensures a coordinated approach to student welfare and safety. Additionally, Residence Life works closely with Public Safety to maintain accurate Clery Act reporting, ensuring that the Clery counts align between both departments. Public Safety provides Residence Life with all reports of incidents occurring within the residence halls. These reports are crucial for informing subsequent student follow-up actions, including conduct-related matters.

Public Safety – Locations, Hours, and Dispatch Operations

Public Safety maintains a presence on both the St. Paul and Minneapolis campuses and operates continuously to keep campus safe 24 hours a day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year.

**St. Paul Campus Location**  
- Office located in Morrison Hall  
- Situated next to Lot B and the baseball field  

**Minneapolis Campus Locations and Hours**  
- Officers are assigned to several desks, including:  
  - Minneapolis School of Law  
  - Terrence Murphy Hall  
  - The Skybox  
  - Minneapolis Opus Hall  
- Minneapolis campus hours: 6:00 AM – 12:00 AM  

**Dispatch Center Operations**  
- The department operates using a centralized Dispatch Center.  
- All calls to Public Safety are routed through Dispatch.  
- Dispatch then sends calls to specific Officers on either the St. Paul or Minneapolis campus.

Public Safety Emergency Call Boxes on Campus

Emergency Call Box stations are located throughout campus to provide quick access to Public Safety in an emergency.

- Each station has a bright blue light on the top and a yellow box on the bottom.
- If you have an emergency and need to speak with Public Safety quickly, press the button on the Call Box.
- When you press the button, Public Safety dispatch will answer and begin gathering information from you.
- At the same time, Public Safety Officers will be dispatched to your location to provide assistance.
- In addition to the outdoor Call Box stations, there are emergency buttons located in restrooms, locker rooms, and several other areas on campus that connect you to Public Safety in the same way.

Emergency Call Box Locations

Emergency Call Boxes are installed in multiple locations across campus to provide quick access to assistance. They are located:

- At designated Emergency Call Box sites around campus.
- On the exterior of most residence halls.

Because of ongoing construction, some Call Boxes may be temporarily disabled or relocated. For this reason, it is important to take note of the exact locations of any Call Boxes you see as you move around campus and near residence halls.

Body-Worn Cameras

We are dedicated to holding our officers to the highest standard, and body‑worn cameras are a key part of that commitment. These cameras support accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement in our response to calls.

Purpose and Use
- Body‑worn cameras allow us to review footage when we need more information for a report.  
- Footage is reviewed if we receive a complaint about how a call was handled.  
- Cameras are also used to debrief officers so we can improve our response and overall practices.  
- Since issuing these cameras to officers, we have seen a significant decrease in complaints.  
- The use of cameras has helped build trust with individuals who may have had poor experiences with law enforcement in the past.

Activation and Recording
- Officers activate body‑worn cameras on every call, including escorts and access requests.  
- The cameras are always buffering (pre‑recording). When activated, they save all video footage from up to 2 minutes prior to activation.  

Indicator Lights
- A red blinking light means the camera is actively recording.  
- A solid green light means the camera is buffering (pre‑recording) but not yet actively recording.
